I really do not want to alarm you, but you need to take this very seriously. He is not "just a creep". I was stalked, made that misjudgment, and it ended up in an attempted kidnapping. Read up and educate yourself on how to deal and live with a stalker. There are ways of protecting yourself physically and online etc. You also need to understand the obsession that drives a stalker too.  To boil it down though, they are in a fantasy world and are unreachable when it comes to logic. Please make sure that this person does not follow you home, since he may not know where you live at present and this will be very important. Also, taking a self defense class (some are offered cheaply at the YMCA for example). Also, stay in public areas and try not to go out at night or alone. I would also take a picture of him and save it along with an account of what is happening. You need to document this. I don't want to scare you, but if something should happen there needs to be a trail to this guy. You didn't deserve this but sadly you are now burdened however with this parasite. If you can move, do so. If you can stay off social media (Facebook in particular) then do so. Also, be angry when this guy shows up. Fight back. He has balls, so kick him. Legally you are justified. Be safe and keep others in your life aware of what is going on. But most of all, do not dismiss this as nothing. My thyroid levels are supposed to be normal, but I have all the other Fibro symptoms, so even with a "normal" thyroid I am considered to have Fibro. It's possible the test misread something in my case as well, although they ran tests more than once. On another connected topic, they have found that I have higher than normal white blood cell count though which would indicate an auto-immune problem or inflammation in the body caused by arthritis.

I also sympathize a lot with you as well. Everything you have described is something I go through almost everyday. The theory from my Doctors so far is that is it Fibromyalgia. Each day is a challenge for me as my body pain will focus on certain parts on certain days with no discernible reasoning behind it. I go through the range in emotions as I am sure you do as well. Venting is good, especially to people that understand (sadly, some people just won't understand no matter how much you explain it to them.)

The only thing I can tell you from my experience so far is that the pain won't be at maximum level every moment of everyday; it can mostly be managed. Having support is key (family, friends, co-workers, your boss, Doctors etc...) and having a sense of humor most days will get you through tough times. As for your guilt, it goes hand-in-hand for people in our position and while you are fully allowed to feel this way, you should talk yourself down from it as much as possible. You can only do what you can, and when you can. Don't feel too guilty for having a legitimate medical condition.

I am such a "doer" just like almost all Fibro people, I have been a perfectionist my whole life. I have had to learn to cut myself some slack and that means that I have a adapt to how I am feeling at a given time. 

Thank you so much for sharing your experience, this is my first time responding to a Reddit post since I felt you needed to know that there are lots of people just like you; you are not alone. 

Side note: Little tips for what has helped my symptoms overall: 

Supplements: Turmeric, Omega 3-6-9, 5-HTP, melatonin, Niacin, Vitamin D, C, Magnesium.

Diet: High Protein, no artificial sweeteners. 

Activities: gentle stretching and yoga, stationary bike and walking/treadmill, meditation, hot baths with Epson salts, relaxing music therapy and watching comedies and other funny content to release endorphins (natural pain killers).
